/-!
# Erdős Problem 452

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/452](https://www.erdosproblems.com/452)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos452

open scoped ArithmeticFunction.omega

/-- The greatest length of an interval in $[x,2x]$ on which
$\omega(n) > \log\log n$ everywhere. -/
noncomputable def largeOmegaIntervalLength (x : ℕ) : ℕ := by
  classical
  exact Nat.findGreatest
    (fun len ↦ ∃ start, x ≤ start ∧ start + len ≤ 2 * x + 1 ∧
      ∀ n ∈ Finset.Ico start (start + len),
        Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ)) < (ω n : ℝ))
    (x + 1)

/-- Determine the largest length of an interval in $[x,2x]$ on which
$\omega(n) > \log\log n$ everywhere. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_452 : largeOmegaIntervalLength = answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

end Erdos452

reformulations.difference: The source maximizes the size of an interval inside [x,2x]. Lean instead performs a bounded search over lengths of half-open integer intervals, using start + len ≤ 2*x + 1 and the search bound x + 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Finset.Ico start (start + len) contains exactly len integers. For len > 0 it equals the closed integer interval [start,start + len - 1], whose last element is at most 2*x exactly when start + len ≤ 2*x + 1. Every admissible length is at most x + 1. Length zero is always admissible, so Nat.findGreatest returns an attained maximum rather than an unintended default. The scratch file proves the equivalence with closed intervals and the maximum characterization.
